title: Instrumental 6: За, Под, Над, Перед (Position)
description: Position prepositions за / под / над / перед take the instrumental for STATIC location: за столом, под стулом, над окном.
descriptionRussian: Предлоги за, под, над, перед в значении статичного положения требуют творительного падежа.
intro: Four prepositions of position, and one of them behaves differently depending on the verb. Sitting behind a table and sitting down behind a table use different cases in Russian, because the language distinguishes being somewhere from arriving there. That contrast is the whole difficulty here; the rest is one ending applied four times.
rules: За (behind, at), под (under), над (above), перед (in front of) take the INSTRUMENTAL case for static position: за столом, под стулом, над окном, перед домом.
Critical contrast: 'за' takes ACCUSATIVE for motion (сесть за стол = sit DOWN at the table) but INSTRUMENTAL for static location (сидеть за столом = sit at the table, ongoing).
The verb determines the case: motion verbs (сесть, лечь, пойти) → accusative; stative verbs (сидеть, лежать, стоять, висеть) → instrumental.
Над (above) and перед (in front of) take ONLY the instrumental: there is no separate motion form, because 'above' and 'in front of' describe positions, not destinations.
Между (between) also takes the instrumental, usually with a plural complement: между домом и школой (between the house and the school).
examples: Антон сидит за столом. (Anton sits at the table.) стол → столом.
Кошка спит под стулом. (The cat sleeps under the chair.) стул → стулом.
Дом стоит за школой. (The house stands behind the school.) школа → школой.
Маша работает над проектом. (Masha is working on her project.) проект → проектом.
Лена стоит перед окном. (Lena stands in front of the window.) окно → окном.

items.hint: Static sitting (no motion) → which case after за?
items.explanation: Сидеть is stative; with за it takes the instrumental: за столом. The accusative 'за стол' would mean motion (Anton sat down at the table = сел за стол). The verb decides the case.

items.promptEnglish: The cat is under the chair.
items.hint: Static location (the cat is, not the cat moves to) → which case after под?
items.explanation: Под for static location takes the instrumental: стул → стулом. Like за, под also has a motion sense ('кошка побежала под стул' = ran under the chair, acc), but the static reading here picks instrumental.

items.promptEnglish: The house stands behind the school.
items.hint: Стоит is stative. Школа is feminine -а.
items.explanation: Стоит is stative; за + instr for location → школой. Школа is feminine -а → -ой. The form школу (acc) would appear with motion ('пошёл за школу' = went behind the school).

items.promptEnglish: Masha is working on her project.
items.hint: Над has no motion form. What case must it take?
items.explanation: Над takes only the instrumental: над проектом. The figurative 'work on (a project)' uses the same над + instr structure as the literal 'hang above (a table)'. Над has no accusative version.

items.promptEnglish: Lena sits in front of the window.
items.hint: Перед is also instrumental-only. Окно is neuter -о.
items.explanation: Перед takes only the instrumental: перед окном. Окно is neuter -о, which (like masculine consonant) takes -ом → окном. Same ending, different gender.

blanks: За _____ парк. (Behind the house there is a park.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: За + instrumental for static location: дом → домом. The sentence reads 'Behind the house [is] a park.'

minimalPairs.explanation: Stative сидеть takes за + instrumental: за столом. The form стол (nom / acc) would only fit a motion construction: 'Антон сел за стол' (Anton sat DOWN at the table, with motion).

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: The house stands behind the school.
minimalPairs.explanation: Стоит is stative; за + instrumental for location → школой. The nominative школа would only mark a subject ('Школа большая.' / 'The school is big.'), not the place behind which the house stands.

errorCorrection.explanation: Сидеть is a stative verb, so за takes the instrumental for static location: за столом. The accusative за стол would mark motion ('сел за стол' = sat DOWN at the table).

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: The cat is sleeping under the sofa.
errorCorrection.explanation: Спит is stative. Под for static location takes the instrumental: под диваном. The accusative под диван would mean motion ('кошка побежала под диван' = ran under the sofa).

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Masha is working on her project.
errorCorrection.explanation: Над takes only the instrumental, in both its literal sense and the figurative 'work on' (работать над чем): проект → проектом. Над проект leaves the bare nominative, which cannot follow a preposition.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Lena stands in front of the school.
errorCorrection.explanation: Перед takes only the instrumental. Школа is feminine -а → -ой → школой. Перед школа leaves the bare nominative, which is never used after a preposition.

errorCorrection.sentence: Антон вошёл и сразу сел за столом.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Anton came in and immediately sat down at the table.
errorCorrection.explanation: The verb decides the case after за. Сесть (to sit DOWN) is a motion verb, so it takes за + ACCUSATIVE: сел за стол (motion into position). За столом (instrumental) marks STATIC location and pairs with stay-put verbs ('сидит за столом', is sitting at the table).

errorCorrection.sentence: Магазин находится между банком и аптеку.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: The store is located between the bank and the pharmacy.
errorCorrection.explanation: Между (between) takes the instrumental, and it applies to BOTH nouns it joins: между банком и аптекой. Банком is already instrumental; the error is аптеку, the accusative. The instrumental of аптека (feminine -а) is аптекой.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: The journalist worked on the article for a long time.
errorCorrection.explanation: Над takes only the instrumental, including the figurative 'work on' (работать над чем). Статья is feminine -я with a stressed ending, so the instrumental is статьёй. Над статью uses the accusative, which над never takes.

reviewVocab.definition: behind, at (takes instrumental for static location, accusative for motion)
in front of (takes only the instrumental)
